343	     7	# Contentful Component Registration
344	     8	
345	     9	Studio Experiences definitions are now **generated from code** — you never write a
346	    10	`defineComponents` entry by hand. The source of truth is the component's `Props` type,
347	    11	annotated with `@cf` JSDoc tags.
348	    12	
349	    13	## Steps
350	    14	
351	    15	### 1. Move the component into `experiences/`
352	    16	
353	    17	The codegen only processes files under
354	    18	`overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/`. If the component isn't there yet,
355	    19	move it (or create it) in that folder.
356	    20	
357	    21	### 2. Add `/** @cf-register */` to the component
358	    22	
359	    23	Place it immediately before the component's `const` declaration:
360	    24	
361	    25	```tsx
362	    26	/** @cf-register */
363	    27	const MyComponent = ({ ... }: MyComponentProps) => { ... };
364	    28	
365	    29	export default MyComponent;
366	    30	```
367	    31	
368	    32	### 3. Annotate every prop in the `Props` type
369	    33	
370	    34	Props without a `@cf` tag are silently skipped — omitting the tag is how you exclude a prop from the Contentful definition.
371	    35	
372	    36	```tsx
373	    37	type MyComponentProps = {
374	    38	  /** @cf Headline */
375	    39	  headline: string;
376	    40	
377	    41	  /** @cf Body Copy, longText */
378	    42	  body?: string;
379	    43	
380	    44	  /** @cf Hero Image, media */
381	    45	  heroImage?: string;
382	    46	
383	    47	  /** @cf Layout, select */
384	    48	  layout?: 'left' | 'right';
385	    49	
386	    50	  internalId?: string;
387	    51	};
388	    52	```
389	    53	
390	    54	**Tag syntax:**
391	    55	
392	    56	| Tag | Meaning |
393	    57	|-----|---------|
394	    58	| `/** @cf Display Name */` | Infer control from the TS type (see table below) |
395	    59	| `/** @cf Display Name, control */` | Override the inferred control |
396	    60	
397	    61	Props without any `@cf` tag are silently skipped — no tag needed to exclude a prop.
398	    62	
399	    63	**Type → control inference table:**
400	    64	
401	    65	| TypeScript type | Inferred control | Contentful variable type |
402	    66	|----------------|-----------------|--------------------------|
403	    67	| `string` | `shortText` | Text |
404	    68	| `boolean` | `toggle` | Boolean |
405	    69	| `number` | `number` | Number |
406	    70	| string literal union (`'a' \| 'b'`) | `select` | Text |
407	    71	
408	    72	**Valid explicit controls:** `shortText`, `longText`, `select`, `toggle`, `number`, `media`
409	    73	
410	    74	**Auto-skipped:** props starting with `on` (event handlers), `children` (emits
411	    75	`children: true` on the component registration instead), and any prop with no `@cf` tag.

417	    81	```

1	# Styling an Override Component
2	
3	How to style a component under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/theme/`.
4	Cross-references [overrides.md](./overrides.md) (module-replacement correctness — a
5	different concern: that file is about not breaking SFCC's own imports, this one is
6	about what values to reach for once the component compiles). Day-to-day CSS/token
7	rules live in [css.md](./css.md); this file is the practical "what do I actually type"
8	companion.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## The hierarchy — reach for these in order
13	
14	1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual. `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`.
15	   All 22 Handover text styles are registered in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`.
16	2. **Raw `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties** for colour and spacing — `color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`,
17	   `bg="var(--zimm-color-bg-02)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`. **Never** a bare Chakra/theme
18	   token string (`color="text.default"`, `gap="m"`) — even though `theme.colors`/`theme.space`
19	   ARE registered from the same Zimmermann foundations (see `theme/index.ts`'s own comment on
20	   which scales are and aren't registered) and a bare key resolves to the identical value. This
21	   is a house-style requirement, not a correctness one: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference is
22	   unambiguous at every call site, where a bare key forces a PR reviewer to check
23	   `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct. Mechanically
24	   enforced across every recipe file by `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s "no
25	   override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale" test — it walks the
26	   registered recipe map only, so it cannot see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop (see
27	   that test's SCOPE note); apply the same discipline there by hand.
28	3. **A component's own theme config** — either centralized (`theme/components/<name>.ts`)
29	   or, per the co-location pattern below, beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — for
30	   anything that needs to vary by variant/size/state and isn't already a Chakra prop — see
31	   "Component-local tokens" and "Co-locating a component's theme file" below. For an
32	   interactive component with existing Chakra support (buttons, inputs, etc.), this theme
33	   config is the single source of truth — see "One canonical styling surface per component
34	   type" below.
35	4. **`sx` prop** for a one-off Chakra-prop-system gap, per [css.md](./css.md).
36	5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` genuinely can't express it (complex pseudo-selectors,
37	   keyframes) — same file, same rules as [css.md](./css.md) already documents.
38	
39	**Never**: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file — reach for the token
40	instead. The one standing exception is `zimmButton.css.ts`'s provisional height/padding
41	constants (`BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`), pending UI-designer
42	sign-off — see Units below. Run `npm run audit:tokens` (`node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`)
43	before opening a PR that touches `overrides/app/components/**` or
44	`overrides/app/theme/components/**` — it greps for exactly this, scoped to those two paths
45	(`.ts`/`.tsx`/`.scss`, excluding `*.test.ts(x)` and `*.stories.tsx`). A match is downgraded
46	from a failure to an acknowledged exception when the surrounding comment block already
47	contains `provisional`, `pending`, `placeholder`, or an explicit `audit-allow: <reason>` —
48	the exact vocabulary this codebase already uses for its documented raw-value exceptions, so
49	existing well-commented code doesn't need a second, separately-maintained allow-list. Built
50	2026-08-23 — it is not wired into CI yet, deliberately: someone still needs to own triaging a
51	full run's worth of pre-existing findings first (a first run against this repo surfaced 14
52	genuine pre-existing violations, none touched by that session, all outside its scope to fix).
53	Note this is a *different, broader* check than `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token-key guard
54	mentioned above: that one exists and runs today (`npm run test`), but only catches a bare
55	Chakra key standing in for a zimm var — it says nothing about a raw hex/px/rem/em literal,
56	which is what `audit:tokens` is for.
57	
58	## Units
59	
60	- **`rem`** for anything that should scale with the user's root font-size / browser zoom
61	  (WCAG 1.4.4): type (`fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`) and spacing
62	  (`spacing.ts`'s named scale). Letter-spacing values that were specified as sub-pixel px
63	  in the source don't round to clean rem numbers, so those keep a trailing `// -0.12px`
64	  comment for traceability.
65	- **`px`** for hairline geometry that should _not_ scale: border widths, focus-ring
66	  offsets, and (for now) the provisional button-height constants in `zimmButton.css.ts` that are
67	  still pending UI-designer sign-off against Handover.
68	- **`em`** only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts` — deliberate, so `.zimm-grid`'s media
69	  queries shift with zoom the same way Chakra's responsive props do) and other
70	  genuinely context-relative cases. Not a general-purpose unit.
71	
72	## The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy
73	
74	`theme/foundation/colour.ts`'s primitive tier (`grey`, `ivory`, ...) is defined first as
75	plain `const`s, and the semantic/alias tier below it (`text`, `background`, `border`,
76	...) reads from those consts (`text.default: grey[900]`) instead of retyping the hex
77	value. Do the same for any new primitive/alias pair you add — two values can't disagree
78	if only one of them is ever typed.
79	
80	`zimmTokens.ts` (the `--zimm-*` CSS-var registry for `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*`
81	classes) is fully derived the same way — it imports `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSizes`/
82	`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/`fontWeights`/`iconSizes`/`actionSizes`/`motion`/`grid`
83	from their owning files rather than retyping values. The only literals left are the 7
84	numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases with no named-scale equivalent (`025`, `700`, `1100`,
85	`1200`, `1300`, `3500`, `4500`) — not duplicates, just Handover values with nothing to
86	derive them from. `theme/index.test.tsx`'s collision-guard tests still exist as a
87	regression net; treat a failure there as a real drift signal, not test noise.
88	
89	## One canonical styling surface per component type
90	
91	Only one place should define how a given interactive component looks: its theme config —
92	either centralized as `theme/components/<name>.ts` or, per the co-location pattern below,
93	beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — consumed via Chakra's component (`<Button>`,
94	`<Link>` variant, etc.). Don't also give it a `.zimm-*` global class in
95	`globalStyles.ts` — a static CSS class can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/
96	`_focusVisible` states the way a Chakra theme config can, so a class "mirror" is
97	structurally incomplete from the start, and nothing stops its values from disagreeing
98	with the real theme config over time. `zimmButton.css.ts` (co-located at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/`) is the single source of truth for
99	button styling; `globalStyles.ts` has no `.zimm-btn-*` classes — use Chakra's `<Button>`
100	for any button, not a class.
101	
102	`.zimm-*` classes remain the right tool for genuinely static, non-interactive,
103	massively-reused treatments (typography, the responsive grid, form-field layout) where
104	there's no interactive state to lose.
105	
106	## Importing an already-overridden component from a new component
107	
108	If component A (e.g. `productDetailOptions`) uses component B, and B already has an
109	override (e.g. `swatch-group`), **import B via a relative path
110	(`'../swatch-group'`), not the SFCC base path
111	(`'@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group'`)** — even though the
112	base path is exactly what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) requires _inside_ an override
113	that's itself shadowing an SFCC module (see `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
114	import, which is correct for that file).
115	
116	The reason the two cases differ: the resolver that redirects
117	`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to `overrides/` (`ccExtensibility` in
118	`package.json`, read by a webpack plugin) only runs in the **real app build** — dev
119	server and production. `.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to
120	`node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it at all, so neither loads the
121	resolver. A base-path import of an already-overridden component will build and run
122	correctly in the shipped app, but silently render/test the **unstyled base SFCC
123	version** in Storybook and Vitest — the story or test looks like it's exercising your
124	override and isn't.
125	
126	**Known instance of this, not yet fixed:** `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
127	import uses the base path. Currently dormant only because its Storybook story exercises
128	the `CardBaseline` named export (which takes `price` as a pre-rendered node and never
129	calls `DisplayPrice`), not the default `ProductTile` bridge that actually renders it —
130	worth fixing before anything writes a story/test against the default export.
131	
132	An override component's own base-path imports (of modules it is _not_ also
133	overriding) are unaffected by this — `RecommendedProducts`, `Seo`, `QuantityPicker`
134	etc. have no local override to miss, so the base path is simply correct for them.
135	
136	## Component-local tokens
137	
138	When a component needs a spacing/sizing value that already has a `spacing.ts` /
139	`iconSizes` / etc. entry, reference that entry **as a `var(--zimm-*)` custom property**
140	— `marginBottom: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)'`, not `marginBottom: 2`, not
141	`marginBottom: '0.5rem'`, and **not** the bare key `marginBottom: 'xs'`. The bare-key
142	form resolved correctly against the registered `theme.space` and was what this section
143	used to recommend, but hierarchy point 2 above now forbids it and
144	`theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token guard **fails the build on it** —
145	so following the old advice inside a registered recipe breaks `npm run test`.
146	
147	See `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts` and
148	`.../footer/bottomBar/bottomBar.css.ts` for the pattern in a real recipe. The reason is
149	traceability, not parity with the base theme: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference names the
150	Figma token it came from, where a raw `2` or `'0.5rem'` names nothing. (Note these
151	recipes are deliberately namespaced `ZimmFooter*` so they do **not** inherit the base
152	SFCC `Footer` config — their values come from Figma, not from re-expressing base
153	numerics. See `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s namespacing guard.)
154	
155	**Responsive steps are explicit media queries, not Chakra's array shorthand.** A
156	co-located recipe keys them off `BP` in `theme/components/footerShared.ts`, in the form:
157	
158	```ts
159	[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)' },
160	```
161	
162	The array shorthand (`['2xs', '2xs', 'xs', 'xs']`) is what this section used to
163	recommend, and it would put a bare token key back at every step — the guard walks
164	responsive arrays and attributes each element to the same prop, so all four fail.
165	`footer.css.ts`'s `contentRow` and `linksInner` parts are the reference.
166	
167	When a component needs a dimension with **no existing foundation entry** (and you don't

## 2. The 11 rules files

### `overrideStyling.md` (280 lines) — the authority on the build approach

The single most prescriptive file. **The styling hierarchy, in reach-for order (`:12-37`):**
1. `textStyle` prop for anything textual — `textStyle="body2"`, **never a raw `fontSize`**; all 22 Handover text styles live in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`.
2. **Raw `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties** for colour and spacing — `color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`. **Never a bare Chakra/theme token key** (`color="text.default"`, `gap="m"`) even though it resolves identically — house-style, for unambiguity at the call site. Mechanically enforced for recipes by `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`; **that guard cannot see the same mistake in a JSX/`sx` prop** — that half is manual (`:24-27`).
3. The component's own theme config — `theme/components/<name>.ts` **or** co-located `<name>.css.ts`.
4. `sx` for a one-off prop-system gap.
5. Scoped `.scss` only when `sx` genuinely can't express it (complex pseudo-selectors, keyframes).

**"Never: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file"** (`:39`). One standing exception: `zimmButton.css.ts`'s provisional `BTN_HEIGHT_LG/SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`. `npm run audit:tokens` (`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`) greps for exactly this across `overrides/app/components/**` and `overrides/app/theme/components/**`; a hit is downgraded when the surrounding comment contains `provisional|pending|placeholder|audit-allow: <reason>`. **Not wired into CI** (`:50`, restated `:227-237`) — 14 pre-existing violations need triage first.

**Units (`:58-70`):** `rem` for anything scaling with root font-size (type + spacing, WCAG 1.4.4); `px` for hairline geometry that must *not* scale (borders, focus-ring offsets); `em` only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts`).

Other hard constraints:
- **Alias tier is a reference, not a copy** (`:72-87`) — semantic tokens read from primitive consts; `zimmTokens.ts` derives everything except 7 numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases.
- **One canonical styling surface per component type** (`:89-104`) — a component's theme config is the single source of truth; **do not also give it a `.zimm-*` global class**, because a static class can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/`_focusVisible`. `globalStyles.ts` has no `.zimm-btn-*`; use Chakra `<Button>`.
- **Importing an already-overridden component (`:106-134`) — a real trap.** From component A, import an already-overridden B by **relative path** (`'../swatch-group'`), *not* the SFCC base path, because the `ccExtensibility` resolver only runs in the real app build — Storybook aliases straight to `node_modules` and Vitest doesn't touch it, so a base-path import silently renders/tests the **unstyled base SFCC version**. Known unfixed instance: `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice` import (`:126-130`).
- **Component-local tokens (`:136-165`)** — reference the foundation entry as `var(--zimm-*)`, not `2`, not `'0.5rem'`, not the bare key. **Responsive steps are explicit media queries keyed off `BP`, not Chakra's array shorthand** — the guard walks responsive arrays and fails every element. No existing foundation entry and no confirmed Figma value → **leave it inherited; don't invent a number**.
- **SFCC bridge pattern (`:173-193`)** — if SFCC's own base components import it, the default export stays a faithful undecorated port (full prop surface, same `forwardRef`); Zimmermann styling goes behind a named export (the `product-tile` `CardBaseline` split).
- **Co-location governance (`:197-250`)** — `theme/components/` is Tier 2 gated to the UI designer, but CODEOWNERS' `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` routes a co-located recipe to the owning squad only, dropping the designer gate. Explicit **known inconsistency flagged not resolved** (`:218-225`): `zimmButton.css.ts`'s unapproved provisional constants are no longer designer-gated while still keying the app-wide `Button` recipe. Cross-file shared values go in a small module that stays in `theme/components/` (e.g. `footerShared.ts`).

## 3. `.claude/hooks/`

Wired in `settings.json:2-61`. Five hooks total — four scripts plus one inline command.

| Event | Matcher | What runs | Blocking? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PreToolUse` | `Write\|Edit\|NotebookEdit` | **Inline command**, `settings.json:9` — `git branch --show-current`; if `develop` or `main`, echoes `BLOCKED: …` and `exit 1` | **Yes — hard block** |
| `PreToolUse` | `Write\|Edit\|NotebookEdit` | `hooks/tier2Warn.sh` | No (`exit 0`) |
| `PostToolUse` | `Write` | Inline: `node_modules/.bin/prettier --write "$f"`, `statusMessage: "Formatting new file with Prettier..."` (`:24-25`) | No |
| `PostToolUse` | `Edit\|Write` | `hooks/contentfulDriftWarn.sh` (`:34`) — **file does not exist**; the `[ -f … ] &&` guard makes it a silent no-op | No |
| `PostToolUse` | `Edit\|Write` | `hooks/registryUpdate.sh` | No |
| `PostToolUse` | `Write` | `hooks/testFileRemind.sh` | No |
| `Stop` | — | `hooks/session-reflect.sh` | **Yes — `decision: "block"`** |

**`tier2Warn.sh` (70 lines)** — parses `tool_input.file_path` from stdin JSON via inline python3, then regex-matches six Tier 2 groups and prints `⚠️ TIER 2 — <group>` + owner + "Required: second developer review before this PR merges to develop." Groups at `:33`, `:40`, `:46`, `:52`, `:58`, `:64`. ⚠️ **The theme branch is broken: `:52` matches `/theme/components/project/`, but `protectedFiles.md:49` defines the Tier 2 path as `overrides/app/theme/components/` — that warning can never fire.** Also missing from the script vs `protectedFiles.md`: `uiCopyProvider/`, `globalStyles.ts`, `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`, `scripts/contentful/`.

**`registryUpdate.sh` (45)** — scoped to `overrides/app/{components,hooks,utils,pages}/` or `overrides/app/routes.*` (`:23-24`); skips `.test.`/`.stories.`/`ContentfulDefinition`; resolves node via PATH → NVM sourcing → newest `~/.nvm/versions/node/*/bin/node`, silently exits if none; then runs `node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs --file="$file_path"` (`:45`). This is what keeps `.claude/registry/` live.

**`testFileRemind.sh` (55)** — scoped to `/app/{components,hooks}/`, JS/TS source only, skips test/spec/stories/ContentfulDefinition. Checks all four `.test.{js,jsx,ts,tsx}` variants and, if none exist, prints `🧪 No test file found for X` + the expected path + **"Run /code-quality to audit test coverage before opening a PR."**

**`session-reflect.sh` (45)** — the most consequential hook. Re-entry guard on `stop_hook_active`; exits early if `git status --porcelain` is empty; otherwise emits `{decision: "block", reason: …}` which **forces Claude to keep working before the session can end**. The instruction: write **a single** proposal file to `.docs/agents-proposals/<ts>-<branch>.md`, and **"Do NOT edit AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .docs/memory/*, .docs/prd/*, or .claude/rules/* directly — those are Tier 1 / human-owned"** (`:28`). Each section must carry target path + rationale tied to something that actually happened + a concrete diff. Candidate list at `:33-42`. If nothing changed, write a one-line "No doc updates proposed." **This is the project's doc-drift mechanism, and it is proposal-only by design.**

## 4. `.claude/registry/`

Five generated markdown tables + two hidden JSON caches. Every `.md` carries the header `> Generated by \`node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs\` — do not edit manually.` plus a timestamp and `> Base: @salesforce/retail-react-app@10.0.0`.

| File | Lines | Columns |
|---|---|---|
| `components.md` | 101 | Component, Origin (Base/Override/Custom), Path, Props, **Tier**, **Squad**, **Consumers**, Last touched, Description |
| `hooks.md` | 71 | Hook, Origin, Path, Description, Consumers, Tier, Squad, Last touched |
| `utils.md` | 39 | Utility, Origin, Path, Exports, Last touched, Description |
| `pages.md` | 25 | Page, Origin, Path, Squad, Tier, Last touched |
| `routes.md` | 26 | URL, Component, Page folder, Source (Override/Inherited), Squad, Tier — generated from `overrides/app/routes.tsx` + inherited base routes |

**Generation** — `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` (header at `:1-16`): full run (`npm run generate:registry`, also run on `postinstall`), incremental `--file=PATH`, or `--fresh` to ignore caches. It scans `overrides/app/` **and** `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/` (`:27-28`), which is why the tables carry `Origin: Base` rows for components that were never overridden. It computes and stamps Tier and Squad onto every row — i.e. the registry is the **materialised join of the tier/squad rules against the actual file tree**.

**Caches:** `.baseCache.json` (52 KB, `{version, schema:3, components:73, hooks:57, utils:30, pages:15}`, rows of `{key,name,path,props,desc,consumers}`) caches the expensive upstream scan. `.overrideCache.json` (6 KB, `{components,hooks,utils}` keyed by repo-relative path → `{hash, consumers, lastTouched}`) uses a **sha1 content hash** so a row's consumer count is only recomputed when its own source actually changed (`generateRegistry.mjs:47-60`). The script's own comment documents a fixed bug where incremental mode used to blank every untouched row in a category to `—`.

**Consumption** — two skills read it and both degrade gracefully: `feature-spec/SKILL.md:39` ("_If `.claude/registry/` exists_, read components.md, hooks.md, utils.md", else `find`), and `generate-changelog/SKILL.md:49-53` (`git diff BASE..HEAD -- .claude/registry/` to detect new assets, else `git log --diff-filter=A`). Its stated purpose (`generateRegistry.mjs:5-7`) is *"structured markdown tables that Claude Code reads instead of grepping the codebase."*
